question: A positive Seidel test — aqueous streaming seen as a dark rivulet through the fluorescein pool under cobalt blue light — indicates a full-thickness corneal wound leak that requires urgent closure.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Positive Seidel test = fluorescein diluted by aqueous leak appearing as a dark rivulet = full-thickness corneal perforation/wound leak. This is a clinical emergency requiring urgent surgical closure.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Seidel test: instil fluorescein 2% → cobalt blue slit-lamp illumination → a positive result shows aqueous diluting the fluorescein as a dark stream (the Seidel sign). Full-thickness leak = urgent repair (suturing or tissue adhesive).
